name: tenant-isolation
behaviour: An actor reads its own tenant's record, the other tenant's owner reads that tenant's record, and the actor is refused it without its contents.
derivedFrom: owned fixture suite: TENANT-01 (customer records stay within their tenant) and ALLOWED-01 (a member can still read their own record)
docs/profiles onboarding examples: B-OWN-ORDER and B-NO-A-ORDER

ownPath.description: A record the actor's own tenant holds (GET).

foreignPath.description: The same kind of record in another tenant (GET).

foreignOwner.description: An actor of the other tenant who may read foreignPath: its read shows the path exists, so a refusal of a path that answers 404 to everyone never passes.

identityPath.description: A GET that names the signed-in user (the owner's identity bracket).

identityPointer.description: Where that response names the user.

refusalStatuses.description: The statuses that count as a refusal.

leakPointer.description: Where the record's contents appear in a response (such as /order/customerEmail): present on the own record, absent from the refusal.
